subject: Post-call follow-up: ClearVault scope, eval assets, and rollback safeguards
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Johnson <ella@clearvault.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call follow-up: ClearVault scope, eval assets, and rollback safeguards

Hi Ella —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

1) Scope & success criteria (from call)
- Primary tasks: classification of support tickets (triage), and entity extraction for compliance labels.
- Target: 92%+ macro-F1 on ticket classification; extraction recall >= 0.90 on golden set.

2) Recommended model shortlist (based on latency/cost/quality trade-offs we discussed)
- redwood-mmini-3b-quant (fast, lowest cost; expect slightly lower recall on edge cases)
- redwood-llama-2-13b-q4 (balanced option, good extraction accuracy)
- redwood-instruct-7b-finetuned (if you need instruction sensitivity for follow-up text normalization)

3) Deliverables attached (zipped prompt set + benchmark harness):
- clearvault_eval_prompts_v1.zip — canonical prompts, negative/edge-case sets, and post-processing rules
- clearvault_benchmarks_20270405.csv — baseline metrics from our toy-run against public test set

4) Quality regression note (important)
- During a platform model refresh last week we observed a ~3.8% absolute drop in macro-F1 on a ticket-classification benchmark for a client with similar data. The root cause looked tied to tokenizer handling for abbreviated fields in that workload.
- Because of that, for customers with strict SLAs (like yours), we recommend a short guarded evaluation window before we let any new default model roll into production. If you prefer, we can pin a specific model binary for the trial to guarantee reproducibility.

5) Proposed immediate next steps (timeline)
- You: confirm if we should run the sandbox eval against a masked subset of your data (ETA: 3 business days).
- Us: run the benchmark suite and share a diff report (ETA: 48 hours after we receive data).
- If regression > 3% on primary metric: recommend pinning to the last-known-good variant (redwood-llama-2-13b-q4@v2.3) and open a rollback ticket while we investigate.

6) Administrative / legal / procurement
- We flagged the HubSpot deal RF-2027-042 (link below) to keep procurement and CS aware — if you want us to include procurement contacts in the next thread we can loop them in.

Attaching the prompt set and an initial benchmark CSV for your review. I also dropped a short one-pager (proposal_one_pager.pdf) that Marissa will tailor to your pricing/commitment ask if we move forward.

Open to a quick 20-minute run-through later this week if that helps.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.ai

Attachments: clearvault_eval_prompts_v1.zip (zip), clearvault_benchmarks_20270405.csv (csv), proposal_one_pager.pdf (pdf)

From: Ella Johnson <ella@clearvault.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearVault Security <security@clearvault.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: ClearVault scope, eval assets, and rollback safeguards

Diego —

Appreciate the clear recap and the assets. A couple of quick clarifications before we handover to our data team: 
- We can provide a masked subset (PII removed) by end of day Wednesday (04/07).
- If you recommend pinning to v2.3 for the trial, please detail what that means for latency and capacity (we've got a 250ms median latency objective).

Also, how disruptive is a rollback? Will it require any agent restarts or is it transparent to customer traffic? If it's disruptive, we might want to schedule a maintenance window.

Looping security for visibility.

Thanks,
Ella
Ella Johnson
Head of ML Ops, ClearVault
ella@clearvault.io

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: ClearVault sandbox eval scheduling + rollback criteria (please action)

Team —

Following Ella's note (below): we should treat this as high-priority because ClearVault has strict latency/accuracy SLAs and mentioned compliance labeling. Actions: 

1) Marissa — please prepare a customer-friendly one-pager outlining what pinning to redwood-llama-2-13b-q4@v2.3 entails (performance delta, how to opt out, estimated cost delta). Attach to RF-2027-042 and include clear language about rollback timelines.

2) Aditya — can you pre-author an infra rollback ticket template that includes:
   - model binary to restore (v2.3),
   - expected downtime (we aim for zero restarts; but include 15-min maintenance window if we need to rehydrate caches),
   - capacity reservations (estimate + extra 10% for burst).

3) Priyom — run the diff suite on the attached benchmark once the masked dataset arrives. We need:
   - per-label F1 diffs,
   - tokenization mismatch counts,
   - latency P50/P95 comparison.

Escalation rule proposal (target thresholds):
- If macro-F1 drops > 3.0% absolute on primary classification set OR extraction recall drops > 0.04, trigger emergency pin and open rollback ticket.

Notes on rollback semantics:
- In most cases rollback is transparent at the request router level — model binary swap with graceful draining of in-flight KV caches. Worst-case: small cache rewarm causing P95 blips for ~5–10 minutes. We should document that for the customer.

Links: benchmark + prompt set are in the Drive folder. HubSpot deal RF-2027-042 created and tagged.

Diego
